newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies called mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies called mostly lower.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures were called mostly lower, up to 0.20 cent per lb lower in hogs and 0.40 cent lower in pork bellies, analysts said.

Steady to lower cash hog prices in Midwest trade Tuesday and possibly follow-through selling from Friday's lower hog and belly futures could weigh on values. Midwest cash dealers said early cash trade was steady to $1.00 per cwt lower because ample hog marketings allowed packers to lower bids.
"I can't see any reason for anybody to step in and buy them (hog futures)," said one analyst, referring to weak cash hog and pork markets.

Although analysts expect pork belly futures to open lower because of recent poor retail demand at fairly lofty prices and continued selling from Friday's sharply lower close, some cautioned that early short covering could produce a higher opening.
USDA quoted 12- to 14-lb cash bellies at $89.00 per cwt in its pork cutout report Friday. Analysts said that is a high price and was probably discouraging retail buying.
